content.value_statement: Event-driven .NET apps need clear Event Grid guidance across topics, domains, namespaces, and CloudEvents. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce practical Azure.Messaging.EventGrid implementation plans.
actual_capabilities: Explain package choices for Event Grid topics, domains, namespaces, and CloudEvents interop.
Draft publisher flows using EventGridPublisherClient with EventGridEvent or CloudEvent payloads.
Guide namespace send, receive, acknowledge, release, and reject workflows.
Show Azure Functions trigger patterns for EventGridEvent and CloudEvent handlers.
Compare EventGridEvent and CloudEvent schemas for .NET event design.
Recommend authentication, batching, idempotency, dead-letter, and schema validation practices.
limitations: It is a static reference skill and does not call Azure APIs.
It does not verify live SDK versions or subscription configuration.
Examples require adaptation for project-specific types, credentials, and RBAC.
It does not replace Azure security, network, or production readiness review.

use_cases.title: Plan Event Publishing
use_cases.description: Design .NET services that publish EventGridEvent or CloudEvent messages to Azure Event Grid topics.

use_cases.title: Choose Event Schemas
use_cases.description: Compare EventGridEvent and CloudEvent tradeoffs before standardizing event contracts.

use_cases.title: Operate Pull Delivery
use_cases.description: Model receive, acknowledge, release, reject, and retry behavior for Event Grid namespace subscriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a First Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me publish one CloudEvent from a .NET service to Azure Event Grid. Include the client choice and required configuration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first publisher.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Consumer Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an Azure Functions handler for EventGridEvent messages. Include parsing, logging, idempotency, and error handling concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Namespace Pull Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET pull delivery workflow for an Event Grid namespace. Include receive, acknowledge, release, reject, and retry behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Event Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Event Grid architecture for topics, domains, namespaces, CloudEvents, authentication, batching, and dead-letter strategy. Identify implementation risks.

output_examples.input: I need to publish order-created events from a .NET service.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering EventGridPublisherClient, CloudEvents, managed identity, batch sending, and retry handling.

output_examples.input: I need to consume events with Azure Functions.
output_examples.output: A handler design that explains trigger choice, event parsing, logging boundaries, idempotency, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: I need pull delivery for an Event Grid namespace.
output_examples.output: A processing workflow that separates receive, acknowledge, release, reject, retry, and dead-letter decisions.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID or managed identity over shared access keys when possible.
Use CloudEvents for new integrations that may need cross-platform interoperability.
Build idempotent handlers and handle partial failures per event.
anti_patterns: Hardcode production access keys or endpoints in sample code or configuration.
Assume Event Grid delivers each event only once.
Treat namespace pull delivery and topic push delivery as the same workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill execute dotnet commands?
faq.answer: No. It documents package commands and helps the AI explain or draft implementation steps.

faq.question: Can it help with CloudEvents?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers CloudEvent publishing, parsing, schema comparison, and Azure Functions trigger usage.

faq.question: Does it support Event Grid namespaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes namespace sender and receiver patterns for pull delivery workflows.

faq.question: Can it choose an authentication method?
faq.answer: It can explain API key, SAS, and Microsoft Entra ID patterns, with managed identity preferred when possible.

faq.question: Will it validate my Azure subscription setup?
faq.answer: No. It cannot inspect live Azure resources, RBAC assignments, or network configuration.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
